findings.title: Kingship as cohesive communal capacity
findings.claim: The making of a people into kings can also be heard as giving the community a cohesive capacity that keeps a collective undertaking standing before the question of territorial possession.
findings.mechanism: The focus result noun مُلُوكًا carries the registered cohesion and sustaining-basis facets. The two جَعَلَ constructions and the placement of prophets فِيكُمْ make the status a capacity conferred within an existing community, while the trusted finding states the cohesion-before-territory relation.
findings.reader_payoff: Kingly status becomes perceptible as a usable communal power that holds direction and continuity, alongside the plain sense of being made rulers.
findings.containment: The ordinary public-kingship reading remains intact. This finding does not decide between historical monarchy, broader authority, or possession, and it makes no claim about a particular territory.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run record names both focus branches at the exact focus occurrence, and the focus surface supplies the result-predicate relation that carries them.

The reader-walk source explicitly states that the bestowed capacity is tested at this threshold.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the remembered status as an entrusted ability that must become action when the command arrives, not merely as an honor attached to the past.
findings.containment: The ordinary claim that God made them kings remains available. The legacy walk does not establish a single historical theory of kingship, and the contraction is carried as a contextual reading rather than a replacement of the focus list.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier and branch records are exact, while the threshold and refusal sequence comes from a legacy reader walk whose context prose is citable as nomination but not as independent target morphology.
